results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Acura NSX, 2019 Acura RDX, RLX and RLX Sport Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Accord, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R and HR-V, 2019-2020 Insight and 2019 Fit vehicles.  The low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: If the fuel pump fails, the engine can stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners and dealers will replace the fuel pump assembly, free of charge.  The recall began July 22, 2020.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2020 Accord Sedan, Accord Hybrid, and 2019-2020 Insight vehicles.  A software error may cause intermittent or continuous disruptions in communication between the Body Control Module (BCM) and other components.  This may result in malfunctions of various systems such as the windshield wipers and defroster, rearview camera, exterior lights, audible warning of a stopped vehicle, and power window operation.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 103, "Windshield Defrosting and Defogging Systems" and number 111, "Rear Visibility" as well as FMVSS numbers 104, 108, 114, 118, and 305.
results.Consequence: Various system malfunctions such as inoperative windshield wipers, defroster, rearview camera, or exterior lighting can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will update the BCM software, free of charge.  The recall is expected to begin February 22, 2021.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's number for this recall is X95.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018 Honda Accord and 2019 Honda Insight vehicles.  In certain scenarios, the back-up camera center display may not function properly.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rearview Mirrors."
results.Consequence: If the rearview camera display does not show what is behind the vehicle, it can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will reprogram the display audio unit software, free of charge.  The recall began October 30, 2018.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are K2G and V2F.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2017-2020 CR-V, 2018-2019 Accord and Accord Hybrid, 2018-2020 Odyssey, 2019 Insight, and 2019-2020 Acura RDX vehicles.  A manufacturing issue with the front seat belts may cause the seat belt buckle channel to interfere with the release button, preventing the seat belt buckle from latching.
results.Consequence: An unlatched seat belt cannot properly restrain the seat occupant during a crash, increasing their risk of injury.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the driver and front passenger seat belt buckle release buttons or the buckle assemblies as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed April 18, 2023.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are NDA, QDB, BDC, MDD, LD9. TDF, FDG, ODH, YDI, ZDE.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2013-2023 Honda Accord, Civic Coupe, Civic Sedan, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R, CR-V, HR-V, Ridgeline, Odyssey, Acura ILX, MDX, MDX Hybrid, RDX, RLX, TLX, 2019-2022 Honda Insight, Passport, 2020 Honda CR-V Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Clarity PHEV, Fit, and 2015-2020 Honda Accord Hybrid, Pilot, Acura NSX vehicles.  The fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: Fuel pump failure can cause an engine stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the fuel pump module, free of charge.  Owner letters were mailed September 6, 2024.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138. results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2021, 2023 Acura TLX, 2019-2024 RDX, 2017-2020, 2022-2026 MDX, 2017-2021, 2023, 2025 Honda Ridgeline, 2017-2022 Pilot, 2019-2021 Passport, 2018-2026 Odyssey, 2019-2022 Insight, 2019-2021 HR-V, 2018-2020 Fit, 2020-2022 CR-V Hybrid, 2017-2022 CR-V, 2017-2018, 2021 Civic Type R, 2017-2021 Civic hatchback, 2016-2020 Civic coupe, 2016-2022 Civic, 2017-2022 Accord Hybrid, and 2016-2022 Accord vehicles. The front passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit, which can cause the air bags to deploy unintentionally during a crash.
results.Consequence: Air bags that deploy unintentionally during a crash increase the risk of injury.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the seat weight sensors, free of charge. Owner notification letters were mailed July 7, 2026. Owners may contact Honda's customer service at 1-888-234-2138. Honda's numbers for this recall are BOL, WO9, OOA, WOM, XOH, NOC, POD, BOE, UOF, POB, EOG, AOI, QO8, TOJ, DO7, and SOK. This recall expands previous NHTSA recall number 24V064. Vehicle Identification Numbers (VINs) involved in this recall will be searchable on NHTSA.gov beginning May 29, 2026.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Acura NSX, 2019 Acura RDX, RLX and RLX Sport Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Accord, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R and HR-V, 2019-2020 Insight and 2019 Fit vehicles.  The low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: If the fuel pump fails, the engine can stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners and dealers will replace the fuel pump assembly, free of charge.  The recall began July 22, 2020.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2020 Accord Sedan, Accord Hybrid, and 2019-2020 Insight vehicles.  A software error may cause intermittent or continuous disruptions in communication between the Body Control Module (BCM) and other components.  This may result in malfunctions of various systems such as the windshield wipers and defroster, rearview camera, exterior lights, audible warning of a stopped vehicle, and power window operation.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 103, "Windshield Defrosting and Defogging Systems" and number 111, "Rear Visibility" as well as FMVSS numbers 104, 108, 114, 118, and 305.
results.Consequence: Various system malfunctions such as inoperative windshield wipers, defroster, rearview camera, or exterior lighting can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will update the BCM software, free of charge.  The recall is expected to begin February 22, 2021.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's number for this recall is X95.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018 Honda Accord and 2019 Honda Insight vehicles.  In certain scenarios, the back-up camera center display may not function properly.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rearview Mirrors."
results.Consequence: If the rearview camera display does not show what is behind the vehicle, it can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will reprogram the display audio unit software, free of charge.  The recall began October 30, 2018.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are K2G and V2F.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2017-2020 CR-V, 2018-2019 Accord and Accord Hybrid, 2018-2020 Odyssey, 2019 Insight, and 2019-2020 Acura RDX vehicles.  A manufacturing issue with the front seat belts may cause the seat belt buckle channel to interfere with the release button, preventing the seat belt buckle from latching.
results.Consequence: An unlatched seat belt cannot properly restrain the seat occupant during a crash, increasing their risk of injury.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the driver and front passenger seat belt buckle release buttons or the buckle assemblies as necessary, free of charge. TDF, FDG, ODH, YDI, ZDE.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

risks.argument: Comparative fault re-allocation: The opposing carrier may argue that the insured's vehicle stalling in a traffic lane constitutes a road hazard the insured had a duty to mitigate (e.g., by moving to the shoulder or activating hazard lights), and may attempt to assign some percentage of fault to the insured to reduce the recoverable demand.

Causation dispute: The carrier may challenge whether the fuel pump failure was the proximate cause of the collision, arguing instead that the third-party driver's inattention was the sole proximate cause, thereby deflecting any recall-based liability theory and limiting exposure to a standard rear-end or lane-strike analysis.

Recall notice defense: Honda may argue that the recall notice was issued and the insured failed to bring the vehicle in for the free remedy in a timely manner, asserting that the insured's failure to complete the recall repair constitutes an intervening act that breaks the chain of causation and reduces or eliminates manufacturer liability.

Causation and component identification: Honda may contest whether the specific fuel pump failure on this VIN was definitively caused by the recall defect versus an independent mechanical failure, requiring expert inspection and documentation to confirm the failed component matches the 20V314000 defect profile.

Damages apportionment: Both the third-party carrier and Honda may argue that the $14,700 demand should be apportioned between them rather than each being jointly and severally liable for the full amount, potentially complicating settlement negotiations and requiring clear documentation of each party's proportionate contribution to the loss.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Acura NSX, 2019 Acura RDX, RLX and RLX Sport Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Accord, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R and HR-V, 2019-2020 Insight and 2019 Fit vehicles.  The low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: If the fuel pump fails, the engine can stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners and dealers will replace the fuel pump assembly, free of charge.  The recall began July 22, 2020.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2020 Accord Sedan, Accord Hybrid, and 2019-2020 Insight vehicles.  A software error may cause intermittent or continuous disruptions in communication between the Body Control Module (BCM) and other components.  This may result in malfunctions of various systems such as the windshield wipers and defroster, rearview camera, exterior lights, audible warning of a stopped vehicle, and power window operation.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 103, "Windshield Defrosting and Defogging Systems" and number 111, "Rear Visibility" as well as FMVSS numbers 104, 108, 114, 118, and 305.
results.Consequence: Various system malfunctions such as inoperative windshield wipers, defroster, rearview camera, or exterior lighting can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will update the BCM software, free of charge.  The recall is expected to begin February 22, 2021.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's number for this recall is X95.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018 Honda Accord and 2019 Honda Insight vehicles.  In certain scenarios, the back-up camera center display may not function properly.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rearview Mirrors."
results.Consequence: If the rearview camera display does not show what is behind the vehicle, it can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will reprogram the display audio unit software, free of charge.  The recall began October 30, 2018.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are K2G and V2F.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2017-2020 CR-V, 2018-2019 Accord and Accord Hybrid, 2018-2020 Odyssey, 2019 Insight, and 2019-2020 Acura RDX vehicles.  A manufacturing issue with the front seat belts may cause the seat belt buckle channel to interfere with the release button, preventing the seat belt buckle from latching.
results.Consequence: An unlatched seat belt cannot properly restrain the seat occupant during a crash, increasing their risk of injury.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the driver and front passenger seat belt buckle release buttons or the buckle assemblies as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed April 18, 2023.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are NDA, QDB, BDC, MDD, LD9. TDF, FDG, ODH, YDI, ZDE.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2013-2023 Honda Accord, Civic Coupe, Civic Sedan, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R, CR-V, HR-V, Ridgeline, Odyssey, Acura ILX, MDX, MDX Hybrid, RDX, RLX, TLX, 2019-2022 Honda Insight, Passport, 2020 Honda CR-V Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Clarity PHEV, Fit, and 2015-2020 Honda Accord Hybrid, Pilot, Acura NSX vehicles.  The fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: Fuel pump failure can cause an engine stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the fuel pump module, free of charge.  Owner letters were mailed September 6, 2024.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are KGC and KGD.  This recall is an expansion of NHTSA recall numbers 21V-215 and 20V-314.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2021, 2023 Acura TLX, 2019-2024 RDX, 2017-2020, 2022-2026 MDX, 2017-2021, 2023, 2025 Honda Ridgeline, 2017-2022 Pilot, 2019-2021 Passport, 2018-2026 Odyssey, 2019-2022 Insight, 2019-2021 HR-V, 2018-2020 Fit, 2020-2022 CR-V Hybrid, 2017-2022 CR-V, 2017-2018, 2021 Civic Type R, 2017-2021 Civic hatchback, 2016-2020 Civic coupe, 2016-2022 Civic, 2017-2022 Accord Hybrid, and 2016-2022 Accord vehicles. liabilityAssessor.output.rationale: The 2018 Honda Accord suffered a fuel pump failure consistent with NHTSA recall campaign 20V314000, causing the vehicle to stall in a live traffic lane on 2026-04-18. The stalled vehicle was then struck by a third-party driver, who was assessed approximately 70% at fault by Officer #8400 in the synthetic police report, making that driver's carrier the primary subrogation target for the collision damages. Because the initiating event was a recalled defective fuel pump component, Honda and/or its recall-responsible party bears concurrent liability as a secondary target for placing the insured in the hazardous stall condition. California's pure comparative negligence doctrine applies, the insured bears 0% fault, and no recovery bar exists — supporting pursuit of the full gross demand of $14,700. The rules engine has confirmed PURSUE status with a 90% probability of recovery and 896 days remaining on the statute of limitations, reflecting strong subrogation potential on both liability theories.

risks.argument: Comparative fault re-allocation: The opposing carrier may argue that the insured's vehicle stalling in a traffic lane constitutes a road hazard the insured had a duty to mitigate (e.g., by moving to the shoulder or activating hazard lights), and may attempt to assign some percentage of fault to the insured to reduce the recoverable demand.

Causation dispute: The carrier may challenge whether the fuel pump failure was the proximate cause of the collision, arguing instead that the third-party driver's inattention was the sole proximate cause, thereby deflecting any recall-based liability theory and limiting exposure to a standard rear-end or lane-strike analysis.

Recall notice defense: Honda may argue that the recall notice was issued and the insured failed to bring the vehicle in for the free remedy in a timely manner, asserting that the insured's failure to complete the recall repair constitutes an intervening act that breaks the chain of causation and reduces or eliminates manufacturer liability.

Causation and component identification: Honda may contest whether the specific fuel pump failure on this VIN was definitively caused by the recall defect versus an independent mechanical failure, requiring expert inspection and documentation to confirm the failed component matches the 20V314000 defect profile.

Damages apportionment: Both the third-party carrier and Honda may argue that the $14,700 demand should be apportioned between them rather than each being jointly and severally liable for the full amount, potentially complicating settlement negotiations and requiring clear documentation of each party's proportionate contribution to the loss.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Acura NSX, 2019 Acura RDX, RLX and RLX Sport Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Accord, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R and HR-V, 2019-2020 Insight and 2019 Fit vehicles.  The low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: If the fuel pump fails, the engine can stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners and dealers will replace the fuel pump assembly, free of charge.  The recall began July 22, 2020.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2020 Accord Sedan, Accord Hybrid, and 2019-2020 Insight vehicles.  A software error may cause intermittent or continuous disruptions in communication between the Body Control Module (BCM) and other components.  This may result in malfunctions of various systems such as the windshield wipers and defroster, rearview camera, exterior lights, audible warning of a stopped vehicle, and power window operation.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 103, "Windshield Defrosting and Defogging Systems" and number 111, "Rear Visibility" as well as FMVSS numbers 104, 108, 114, 118, and 305.
results.Consequence: Various system malfunctions such as inoperative windshield wipers, defroster, rearview camera, or exterior lighting can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will update the BCM software, free of charge.  The recall is expected to begin February 22, 2021.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's number for this recall is X95.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018 Honda Accord and 2019 Honda Insight vehicles.  In certain scenarios, the back-up camera center display may not function properly.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rearview Mirrors."
results.Consequence: If the rearview camera display does not show what is behind the vehicle, it can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will reprogram the display audio unit software, free of charge.  The recall began October 30, 2018.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are K2G and V2F.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2017-2020 CR-V, 2018-2019 Accord and Accord Hybrid, 2018-2020 Odyssey, 2019 Insight, and 2019-2020 Acura RDX vehicles.  A manufacturing issue with the front seat belts may cause the seat belt buckle channel to interfere with the release button, preventing the seat belt buckle from latching.
results.Consequence: An unlatched seat belt cannot properly restrain the seat occupant during a crash, increasing their risk of injury.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the driver and front passenger seat belt buckle release buttons or the buckle assemblies as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed April 18, 2023.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are NDA, QDB, BDC, MDD, LD9. TDF, FDG, ODH, YDI, ZDE.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

The fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.

Damages apportionment: Both the third-party carrier and Honda may argue that the $14,700 demand should be apportioned between them rather than each being jointly and severally liable for the full amount, potentially complicating settlement negotiations and requiring clear documentation of each party's proportionate contribution to the loss.

risks.argument: Comparative fault re-allocation: The opposing carrier may argue that the insured's vehicle stalling in a traffic lane constitutes a road hazard the insured had a duty to mitigate (e.g., by moving to the shoulder or activating hazard lights), and may attempt to assign some percentage of fault to the insured to reduce the recoverable demand.

Causation dispute: The carrier may challenge whether the fuel pump failure was the proximate cause of the collision, arguing instead that the third-party driver's inattention was the sole proximate cause, thereby deflecting any recall-based liability theory and limiting exposure to a standard rear-end or lane-strike analysis.

Recall notice defense: Honda may argue that the recall notice was issued and the insured failed to bring the vehicle in for the free remedy in a timely manner, asserting that the insured's failure to complete the recall repair constitutes an intervening act that breaks the chain of causation and reduces or eliminates manufacturer liability.

Causation and component identification: Honda may contest whether the specific fuel pump failure on this VIN was definitively caused by the recall defect versus an independent mechanical failure, requiring expert inspection and documentation to confirm the failed component matches the 20V314000 defect profile.

Damages apportionment: Both the third-party carrier and Honda may argue that the $14,700 demand should be apportioned between them rather than each being jointly and severally liable for the full amount, potentially complicating settlement negotiations and requiring clear documentation of each party's proportionate contribution to the loss.

risks.argument: Comparative fault re-allocation: The opposing carrier may argue that the insured's vehicle stalling in a traffic lane constitutes a road hazard the insured had a duty to mitigate (e.g., by moving to the shoulder or activating hazard lights), and may attempt to assign some percentage of fault to the insured to reduce the recoverable demand.

Causation dispute: The carrier may challenge whether the fuel pump failure was the proximate cause of the collision, arguing instead that the third-party driver's inattention was the sole proximate cause, thereby deflecting any recall-based liability theory and limiting exposure to a standard rear-end or lane-strike analysis.

Recall notice defense: Honda may argue that the recall notice was issued and the insured failed to bring the vehicle in for the free remedy in a timely manner, asserting that the insured's failure to complete the recall repair constitutes an intervening act that breaks the chain of causation and reduces or eliminates manufacturer liability.

Causation and component identification: Honda may contest whether the specific fuel pump failure on this VIN was definitively caused by the recall defect versus an independent mechanical failure, requiring expert inspection and documentation to confirm the failed component matches the 20V314000 defect profile.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Acura NSX, 2019 Acura RDX, RLX and RLX Sport Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Accord, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R and HR-V, 2019-2020 Insight and 2019 Fit vehicles.  The low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: If the fuel pump fails, the engine can stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners and dealers will replace the fuel pump assembly, free of charge.  The recall began July 22, 2020.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2020 Accord Sedan, Accord Hybrid, and 2019-2020 Insight vehicles.  A software error may cause intermittent or continuous disruptions in communication between the Body Control Module (BCM) and other components.  This may result in malfunctions of various systems such as the windshield wipers and defroster, rearview camera, exterior lights, audible warning of a stopped vehicle, and power window operation.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 103, "Windshield Defrosting and Defogging Systems" and number 111, "Rear Visibility" as well as FMVSS numbers 104, 108, 114, 118, and 305.
results.Consequence: Various system malfunctions such as inoperative windshield wipers, defroster, rearview camera, or exterior lighting can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will update the BCM software, free of charge.  The recall is expected to begin February 22, 2021.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's number for this recall is X95.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018 Honda Accord and 2019 Honda Insight vehicles. As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rearview Mirrors."
results.Consequence: If the rearview camera display does not show what is behind the vehicle, it can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will reprogram the display audio unit software, free of charge.  The recall began October 30, 2018.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are K2G and V2F.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2017-2020 CR-V, 2018-2019 Accord and Accord Hybrid, 2018-2020 Odyssey, 2019 Insight, and 2019-2020 Acura RDX vehicles.  A manufacturing issue with the front seat belts may cause the seat belt buckle channel to interfere with the release button, preventing the seat belt buckle from latching.
results.Consequence: An unlatched seat belt cannot properly restrain the seat occupant during a crash, increasing their risk of injury.

Owner notification letters were mailed April 18, 2023.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are NDA, QDB, BDC, MDD, LD9. risks.argument: Comparative fault re-allocation: The opposing carrier may argue that the insured's vehicle stalling in a traffic lane constitutes a road hazard the insured had a duty to mitigate (e.g., by moving to the shoulder or activating hazard lights), and may attempt to assign some percentage of fault to the insured to reduce the recoverable demand.

Causation dispute: The carrier may challenge whether the fuel pump failure was the proximate cause of the collision, arguing instead that the third-party driver's inattention was the sole proximate cause, thereby deflecting any recall-based liability theory and limiting exposure to a standard rear-end or lane-strike analysis.

Recall notice defense: Honda may argue that the recall notice was issued and the insured failed to bring the vehicle in for the free remedy in a timely manner, asserting that the insured's failure to complete the recall repair constitutes an intervening act that breaks the chain of causation and reduces or eliminates manufacturer liability.

Causation and component identification: Honda may contest whether the specific fuel pump failure on this VIN was definitively caused by the recall defect versus an independent mechanical failure, requiring expert inspection and documentation to confirm the failed component matches the 20V314000 defect profile.

Damages apportionment: Both the third-party carrier and Honda may argue that the $14,700 demand should be apportioned between them rather than each being jointly and severally liable for the full amount, potentially complicating settlement negotiations and requiring clear documentation of each party's proportionate contribution to the loss.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Acura NSX, 2019 Acura RDX, RLX and RLX Sport Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Accord, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R and HR-V, 2019-2020 Insight and 2019 Fit vehicles.  The low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: If the fuel pump fails, the engine can stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners and dealers will replace the fuel pump assembly, free of charge.  The recall began July 22, 2020.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2020 Accord Sedan, Accord Hybrid, and 2019-2020 Insight vehicles.  A software error may cause intermittent or continuous disruptions in communication between the Body Control Module (BCM) and other components.  This may result in malfunctions of various systems such as the windshield wipers and defroster, rearview camera, exterior lights, audible warning of a stopped vehicle, and power window operation.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 103, "Windshield Defrosting and Defogging Systems" and number 111, "Rear Visibility" as well as FMVSS numbers 104, 108, 114, 118, and 305.
results.Consequence: Various system malfunctions such as inoperative windshield wipers, defroster, rearview camera, or exterior lighting can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will update the BCM software, free of charge.  The recall is expected to begin February 22, 2021.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's number for this recall is X95.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018 Honda Accord and 2019 Honda Insight vehicles.  In certain scenarios, the back-up camera center display may not function properly.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rearview Mirrors."
results.Consequence: If the rearview camera display does not show what is behind the vehicle, it can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will reprogram the display audio unit software, free of charge.  The recall began October 30, 2018.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are K2G and V2F.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2017-2020 CR-V, 2018-2019 Accord and Accord Hybrid, 2018-2020 Odyssey, 2019 Insight, and 2019-2020 Acura RDX vehicles.  A manufacturing issue with the front seat belts may cause the seat belt buckle channel to interfere with the release button, preventing the seat belt buckle from latching.
results.Consequence: An unlatched seat belt cannot properly restrain the seat occupant during a crash, increasing their risk of injury.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the driver and front passenger seat belt buckle release buttons or the buckle assemblies as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed April 18, 2023.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are NDA, QDB, BDC, MDD, LD9. TDF, FDG, ODH, YDI, ZDE.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2013-2023 Honda Accord, Civic Coupe, Civic Sedan, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R, CR-V, HR-V, Ridgeline, Odyssey, Acura ILX, MDX, MDX Hybrid, RDX, RLX, TLX, 2019-2022 Honda Insight, Passport, 2020 Honda CR-V Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Clarity PHEV, Fit, and 2015-2020 Honda Accord Hybrid, Pilot, Acura NSX vehicles.  The fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: Fuel pump failure can cause an engine stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the fuel pump module, free of charge.  Owner letters were mailed September 6, 2024.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are KGC and KGD.  This recall is an expansion of NHTSA recall numbers 21V-215 and 20V-314.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2021, 2023 Acura TLX, 2019-2024 RDX, 2017-2020, 2022-2026 MDX, 2017-2021, 2023, 2025 Honda Ridgeline, 2017-2022 Pilot, 2019-2021 Passport, 2018-2026 Odyssey, 2019-2022 Insight, 2019-2021 HR-V, 2018-2020 Fit, 2020-2022 CR-V Hybrid, 2017-2022 CR-V, 2017-2018, 2021 Civic Type R, 2017-2021 Civic hatchback, 2016-2020 Civic coupe, 2016-2022 Civic, 2017-2022 Accord Hybrid, and 2016-2022 Accord vehicles. The front passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit, which can cause the air bags to deploy unintentionally during a crash.
results.Consequence: Air bags that deploy unintentionally during a crash increase the risk of injury.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the seat weight sensors, free of charge. Owner notification letters were mailed July 7, 2026. Owners may contact Honda's customer service at 1-888-234-2138. Honda's numbers for this recall are BOL, WO9, OOA, WOM, XOH, NOC, POD, BOE, UOF, POB, EOG, AOI, QO8, TOJ, DO7, and SOK. This recall expands previous NHTSA recall number 24V064. Vehicle Identification Numbers (VINs) involved in this recall will be searchable on NHTSA.gov beginning May 29, 2026.

The vehicle lost power while in a traffic lane and was subsequently struck by another vehicle, as documented in the synthetic police report by Officer #8400, who attributed approximately 70% fault to the other party. The repair estimate (EST-00017-896, validated by rules engine) confirms the loss cause as "struck in traffic lane after engine stall (fuel pump)," directly corroborating the recall component failure as the initiating event. risks.argument: Comparative fault re-allocation: The opposing carrier may argue that the insured's vehicle stalling in a traffic lane constitutes a road hazard the insured had a duty to mitigate (e.g., by moving to the shoulder or activating hazard lights), and may attempt to assign some percentage of fault to the insured to reduce the recoverable demand.

Causation dispute: The carrier may challenge whether the fuel pump failure was the proximate cause of the collision, arguing instead that the third-party driver's inattention was the sole proximate cause, thereby deflecting any recall-based liability theory and limiting exposure to a standard rear-end or lane-strike analysis.

Recall notice defense: Honda may argue that the recall notice was issued and the insured failed to bring the vehicle in for the free remedy in a timely manner, asserting that the insured's failure to complete the recall repair constitutes an intervening act that breaks the chain of causation and reduces or eliminates manufacturer liability.

Causation and component identification: Honda may contest whether the specific fuel pump failure on this VIN was definitively caused by the recall defect versus an independent mechanical failure, requiring expert inspection and documentation to confirm the failed component matches the 20V314000 defect profile.

Damages apportionment: Both the third-party carrier and Honda may argue that the $14,700 demand should be apportioned between them rather than each being jointly and severally liable for the full amount, potentially complicating settlement negotiations and requiring clear documentation of each party's proportionate contribution to the loss.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2019 Acura NSX, 2019 Acura RDX, RLX and RLX Sport Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Accord, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R and HR-V, 2019-2020 Insight and 2019 Fit vehicles.  The low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: If the fuel pump fails, the engine can stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners and dealers will replace the fuel pump assembly, free of charge.  The recall began July 22, 2020.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2020 Accord Sedan, Accord Hybrid, and 2019-2020 Insight vehicles.  A software error may cause intermittent or continuous disruptions in communication between the Body Control Module (BCM) and other components.  This may result in malfunctions of various systems such as the windshield wipers and defroster, rearview camera, exterior lights, audible warning of a stopped vehicle, and power window operation.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 103, "Windshield Defrosting and Defogging Systems" and number 111, "Rear Visibility" as well as FMVSS numbers 104, 108, 114, 118, and 305.
results.Consequence: Various system malfunctions such as inoperative windshield wipers, defroster, rearview camera, or exterior lighting can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will update the BCM software, free of charge.  The recall is expected to begin February 22, 2021.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's number for this recall is X95.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Component: BACK OVER PREVENTION: SENSING SYSTEM: CAMERA
results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018 Honda Accord and 2019 Honda Insight vehicles.  In certain scenarios, the back-up camera center display may not function properly.  As such, these vehicles fail to comply with the requirements of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) number 111, "Rearview Mirrors."
results.Consequence: If the rearview camera display does not show what is behind the vehicle, it can increase the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Honda will notify owners, and dealers will reprogram the display audio unit software, free of charge.  The recall began October 30, 2018.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are K2G and V2F.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.safercar.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2017-2020 CR-V, 2018-2019 Accord and Accord Hybrid, 2018-2020 Odyssey, 2019 Insight, and 2019-2020 Acura RDX vehicles.  A manufacturing issue with the front seat belts may cause the seat belt buckle channel to interfere with the release button, preventing the seat belt buckle from latching.
results.Consequence: An unlatched seat belt cannot properly restrain the seat occupant during a crash, increasing their risk of injury.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the driver and front passenger seat belt buckle release buttons or the buckle assemblies as necessary, free of charge.  Owner notification letters were mailed April 18, 2023.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138.  Honda's numbers for this recall are NDA, QDB, BDC, MDD, LD9. TDF, FDG, ODH, YDI, ZDE.
results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2013-2023 Honda Accord, Civic Coupe, Civic Sedan, Civic Hatchback, Civic Type R, CR-V, HR-V, Ridgeline, Odyssey, Acura ILX, MDX, MDX Hybrid, RDX, RLX, TLX, 2019-2022 Honda Insight, Passport, 2020 Honda CR-V Hybrid, 2018-2019 Honda Clarity PHEV, Fit, and 2015-2020 Honda Accord Hybrid, Pilot, Acura NSX vehicles.  The fuel pump inside the fuel tank may fail.
results.Consequence: Fuel pump failure can cause an engine stall while driving, increasing the risk of a crash.
results.Remedy: Dealers will replace the fuel pump module, free of charge.  Owner letters were mailed September 6, 2024.  Owners may contact Honda customer service at 1-888-234-2138. results.Notes: Owners may also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 (TTY 1-800-424-9153), or go to www.nhtsa.gov.

results.Summary: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.) is recalling certain 2018-2021, 2023 Acura TLX, 2019-2024 RDX, 2017-2020, 2022-2026 MDX, 2017-2021, 2023, 2025 Honda Ridgeline, 2017-2022 Pilot, 2019-2021 Passport, 2018-2026 Odyssey, 2019-2022 Insight, 2019-2021 HR-V, 2018-2020 Fit, 2020-2022 CR-V Hybrid, 2017-2022 CR-V, 2017-2018, 2021 Civic Type R, 2017-2021 Civic hatchback, 2016-2020 Civic coupe, 2016-2022 Civic, 2017-2022 Accord Hybrid, and 2016-2022 Accord vehicles. The front passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit, which can cause the air bags to deploy unintentionally during a crash.

Recall notice defense: Honda may argue that the recall notice was issued and the insured failed to bring the vehicle in for the free remedy in a timely manner, asserting that the insured's failure to complete the recall repair constitutes an intervening act that breaks the chain of causation and reduces or eliminates manufacturer liability.

Causation and component identification: Honda may contest whether the specific fuel pump failure on this VIN was definitively caused by the recall defect versus an independent mechanical failure, requiring expert inspection and documentation to confirm the failed component matches the 20V314000 defect profile.
